title: Finite scalar extension and the shifted ordinary pullback square
statement: Fix a purity finite setting P [def-pur-conventions], an integer m with 1 <= m <= P.level, its actual derived quotient extension R_T and pullback coefficient comparison p_h [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons]. For arbitrary schemes X,X prime,Y,Y prime in the same universe, let u:X prime -> X, f prime:X prime -> Y prime, f:X -> Y, v:Y prime -> Y form a Cartesian square. Use the ordinary realization pullbacks F_h=P.finiteReductionPullback h and their square c=F_u F_f -> F_fprime F_v from [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]; let G_h and c_B be the same constructions at level m. For every integer r and every ordinary intrinsic derived object K on Y, the following maps from R_Xprime(F_u((F_f K)[r])) to (G_fprime(G_v(R_Y K)))[r] agree: R of the shift comparison of F_u, then R(c_K[r]), then the shift comparison of R_Xprime, then p_fprime(F_v K)[r], then G_fprime(p_v(K))[r]; and p_u((F_f K)[r]), then G_u of the shift comparison of R_X followed by p_f(K)[r], then the shift comparison of G_u, then c_B(R_Y K)[r]. Shift comparisons are the published exact inverse-image shifts and the scalar-adjoint shifts of def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons. There are no twists, roots, exceptional inverse images, or restrictions of smoothness, boundedness, constructibility or Tor amplitude.

proof.text: Use lem-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-cube for the actual coefficient quotient. Its scalar extension and scalar/pullback maps are the ring-sheaf ones in the definition of finiteReductionPullbackComparison. Identify the canonical geometric compositor with exact localization using lem-weil-pbc-ringed-square-localization. The unit-preserving raw pullback models of def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons identify it with the realization compositor: their right mates both restrict sections along the same fibre-product association, so adjunction transposition and the triangle identities give equality. Conjugate the constant-ring cube by these four models. Naturality cancels the models on the internal edges, giving the unshifted ordinary realization cube.

The exact ordinary restriction and pullback functors act termwise on cochain complexes. Their comparison and compositor commute with every integer shift, since the same map is applied in degree i+r and both differentials receive the same sign. Their exact-derived localizations preserve this equality. Scalar extension carries precisely the shift that is adjoint to exact restriction; transposing the shift equation for the restriction/pullback comparison makes its inverse scalar mate commute with the composite shifts. Conjugation by the exact-derived raw pullback models retains this equation. Shift the unshifted cube, expand the composite shifts, and use the coefficient/pullback shift equation on u. Naturality of the scalar shift along the geometric square gives exactly the stated five-factor identity. Shift zero, equal coefficient levels, empty schemes and zero objects obey the same equations. No flatness of the quotient map is used.

theorem finiteReduction_shiftedPullbackCube (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ P.level)
    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (u : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (f : X ⟶ Y) (v : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (sq : IsPullback u f' f v) (r : ℤ) (K : Scheme.proEtaleDerivedCategory Y P.Ring) :
    (P.finiteReduction m hm hmn X').map
        (((P.finiteReductionPullback u).commShiftIso r).hom.app
          ((P.finiteReductionPullback f).obj K)) ≫
      (P.finiteReduction m hm hmn X').map
        ((P.finiteReductionPullbackSquare u f' f v sq K).hom⟦r⟧') ≫
      ((P.finiteReduction m hm hmn X').commShiftIso r).hom.app
        ((P.finiteReductionPullback f').obj ((P.finiteReductionPullback v).obj K)) ≫
      (P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn f'
        ((P.finiteReductionPullback v).obj K)).hom⟦r⟧' ≫
      (((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullback f').map
        (P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn v K).hom)⟦r⟧' =
    (P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn u
        (((P.finiteReductionPullback f).obj K)⟦r⟧)).hom ≫
      ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullback u).map
        (((P.finiteReduction m hm hmn X).commShiftIso r).hom.app
          ((P.finiteReductionPullback f).obj K) ≫
        (P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn f K).hom⟦r⟧') ≫
      (((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullback u).commShiftIso r).hom.app
        (((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullback f).obj
          ((P.finiteReduction m hm hmn Y).obj K)) ≫
      ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullbackSquare u f' f v sq
        ((P.finiteReduction m hm hmn Y).obj K)).hom⟦r⟧'
